text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ruling parties in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation agree to appoint a Croat candidate as the Federation president and a Moslem as the deputy president. The officials will be named at the next federal parliament session.

- The slow implementation of the Bosnian Moslem-Croat Federation's constitution causes delays in the adoption of fundamental laws in the field of financing health care, the federation Health Minister Bozo Ljubic says in response to a new strike threat of unpaid health workers.

- Following information from the German embassy that the Serb co-chairman in Bosnia's Council of Ministers, Boro Bosic, wants to travel separately, the Moslem co-chairman Haris Silajdzic wrote a letter to German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and informed him he cannot make an announced visit to Germany scheduled for January 28, Silajdzic's office said.

- The same Bosnian Serbs who took control of the northwest Bosnian town of Prijedor during the war are still in control over key economic, infrastructural and humanitarian sectors and have normal contacts with international organisations, the Helsinki Human Rights Watch Organisation said on Sunday.

- Prime Minister of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Edhem Bicakcic intends to start a process in which he wants to dismiss his deputy Drago Bilandzija's decision to allow a local company to import goods without paying taxes.
- Two unidentified persons wearing Croat police uniforms robbed two women driving along a highway in southern Bosnia.
- International envoy for divided Bosnian town of Mostar, Sir Martin Garrod, appeals to international and domestic journalists to stop boycotting his office folowing a recent incident.
